passage:
Daycare note, Tuesday. Ayesha.
When snack time ended, Darshan went stiff and red-faced and threw his cup. He tried to hit me too. I moved the cups away, knelt nearby and said, "You're so angry. I'll keep you safe." I didn't punish or lecture. I waited. After a few minutes he crawled into my lap. Then we cleaned up together.

qa.q: What was Darshan feeling when snack time ended?
qa.a: Darshan was furious; his stiff body, red face and throwing show an anger he could not yet control.

qa.q: Why did Ayesha wait instead of punishing?
qa.a: A toddler cannot yet put the brakes on anger, so keeping him safe and staying calm lets the storm pass and teaches more than a punishment.

qa.q: What might Ayesha have felt when Darshan tried to hit?
qa.a: Ayesha may have felt startled, yet stayed steady and kept Darshan safe rather than taking it personally.

grounding: A toddler's fury shows as a stiff body, a red face, throwing and hitting, and is met with calm, safety and waiting rather than punishment.

passage: At the temple fair in their village, two-year-old Ritu wanted the red balloon and was told no. Her body went rigid, her face turned red, and she flung her slipper at the stall. An old man muttered, "One smack and she'll stop." Her mother, Vinita, only scooped her away from the busy lane, sat on the temple step and held her loosely. "You're so cross. I'm here." Ritu kicked and wailed, then slowly slumped against her.

qa.q: What did Ritu fling at the stall?
qa.a: Ritu flung her slipper at the stall.

qa.q: What was Ritu feeling when she was told no?
qa.a: Ritu was furious; her rigid body and red face show an anger she had no way yet to stop.

qa.q: Why was Vinita's response wiser than the old man's suggestion?
qa.a: Vinita kept Ritu safe from the busy lane and waited calmly, letting the anger pass instead of adding fear with a smack.

qa.q: How does the old man see Ritu's outburst?
qa.a: The old man sees it as naughtiness to be stopped with a smack, not as a small child overwhelmed by anger.

grounding: A toddler's anger shows as stiffness, a red face and throwing, and is handled by keeping the child safe, staying calm and waiting.
